channel.title: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet." - Are We Cool Yet? No, we're pretentious wankers.

item.title: Re: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.
item.content:encoded:
I should make it clear that the article itself isn't meant to be a parody, in-universe it's just a regular foundation document like any other. The statue itself is a disillusioned AWCY creating something to mock AWCY. Essentially saying they're all just psychopaths making harmful objects and justifying it with a bunch of bullshit about creating 'art'. I don't picture the artist responsible as trying to be funny really, but mocking the organisation he is/was apart of.

Now that I think about it, it's sort of the reverse of -1802, the AWCY robot that makes fun of the foundation.

And I do realise now that the concept does make the foundation look pretty incompetent. I think the statue killing one or two people before the foundation ramps up its precautions would fit a lot better, and for there to be a solid reason why the foundation tries to find out what the piece is saying. I'm currently mulling over what exactly convinces the foundation to try and 'interpret' the work rather than lock it away completely, and I'm thinking maybe it's just the one senior researcher who has a background in anomalous art and becomes obsessed with the piece, perhaps his personal notes are the things being partially logged in the article.

As to your second-last paragraph @cybersqyd - that sounds like a really interesting SCP idea for a much better writer than me, I don't think my ability extends to deep-dive analysis of art history.

item.title: Re: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

matching the actual effects of the statue becoming more nonsensical and racking up a larger body count in the process. Eventually the statue starts just killing people at random for seemingly no reason

I'm a little hesitant about this aspect because like….it feels like the Foundation should be better equipped to handle this?

the foundation eventually works out that they have inadvertently been led on a wild goose chase, and deduce the item was meant as a parody of AWCY themselves

this feels…perhaps odd to me; like…I kinda get how this works as a parody of AWCY? but it feels like, the whole angle of it leading the foundation on a wild goose chase feels like the actual parody angle of the object is too subtle in universe: like, generally if you're doing a parody, you want people to know it's a parody and enjoy it as such; rather than to trick them into reacting like it's real right up until you pull the curtain back and go 'sike', y'know?

Part of me also feels like the Foundation is a lot more likely to ask 'how do we get this to stop' than 'what is the artist trying to say' and I'm a little unsure of the focus here as a result.

I think there's a small part of me that feels like doing a genuinely confusing artistic piece sincerely; like, the kind of anart piece that genuinely defies meaning and which the foundation attempts to understand the why of might be more interesting than treating it as a parody of AWCY?; and like, having this as an exploration of what art is would be more interesting but *shrugs*.

Alternatively: the idea of this being a thing to make fun of AWCY? feels actually fun and I think taking this in a lot more comedic route could help; where like, instead of being just 'a bunch of actual AWCY? things slapped together weirdly', it's like, a deliberately incompetently done piece? Where you actually like, play up the comedy a lot more and deliberately make this a funny article about a weird thing: like almost using the classic comedy duo thing of the SCP being the comedy provider and the Foundation being the straight man, y'know?

item.title: Re: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.
item.content:encoded:
I like the concept of an AWCY parody, it certainly feels like something they’d do. But at the same time this doesn’t seem much like a parody. Most of what I’m seeing here is various tropes collecting together. You have unnecessary violence:

Eventually the statue starts just killing people at random for seemingly no reason, before stopping completely.

You have the cruel Foundation:

kidnapping and interrogating AWCY members

Tropes are all well and good for parodies. But my problem is that if I were reading this, I wouldn’t think, “neat, this person’s parodying various SCP tropes.” I would think, “why is this such a cliche SCP?” I think the main problem is that you have inconsistent abilities for the statue. With the strange set of powers you’ve given it I see no good way for you to properly explain to the reader that the researcher’s behavior is caused by the statue.

Overall, I like the idea of a parody SCP like this and you seem to be on the right track. But I think you’d face significant problems when trying to communicate the idea to the reader with the properties you’re using now.

item.title: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

-Anomalous statue with "Are We Cool Yet" carved into the bottom. Occasionally 'activates', creating a memetic aura causing a variety of effects in people around them. Note attached, filled with nonsensical writing "explaining" the artistic significance of the statue. The effects are assumed by the Foundation to be some kind of pretentious commentary, as most AWCY projects are, and try to figure out what it all means in an attempt to stop its effects or discover its creator.

-Is eventually revealed to be an in-universe parody of AWCY, likely made by a member of ACWY as a sort of self-own after it stops its effects and is reclassified as neutralised.

Central Narrative:

-Foundation attempts to interpret the effects of the statue, researching increasingly obscure art pieces and reaching more and more in an attempt to work out what the artist was trying to say.

-One of the statues effects makes the researchers think the statue is prophesying some catastrophic event, fuelled by their own (justified, at this point) paranoia, and begin kidnapping and interrogating AWCY members to no avail.

+ show block
– hide block

-Their interpretations become ridiculously complex in a search for some kind of cohesive meaning, matching the actual effects of the statue becoming more nonsensical and racking up a larger body count in the process. Eventually the statue starts just killing people at random for seemingly no reason, before stopping completely.

-Item is reclassified as "Safe" or "neutralized" and the foundation eventually works out that they have inadvertently been led on a wild goose chase, and deduce the item was meant as a parody of AWCY themselves- meaningless effects resulting in unnecessarily deaths and a note pretentiously explaining the work.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

-The items effects are extremely weird and nonsensical, and the foundation's interpretations of the items effects cross-link other SCP's and reference various societal or historical events, phenomenon, and art pieces.

-As far as I could tell there aren't any AWCY scips that directly make fun of their own group, which seems something right up their alley.

Additional Notes:

-Started as a GAW project, but I prefer it as an actual AWCY member making fun of the group he's apart of.
